Who this worksheet is for

This worksheet helps Year 9 learners understand factorising as the reverse of expanding, beginning with numerical factors and progressing to factors containing letters.

Four lesson and exercise pages are followed by two solution pages. Exercises include missing expressions, error spotting and an independent check, alongside teaching notes.

6 pages · Examples, practice & solutions

What the worksheet covers

  • Taking out common numerical factors
  • Common factors involving letters and powers
  • Choosing the greatest common factor to factorise fully
  • Dividing every term and checking by expansion
  • Finding mistakes and completing missing expressions

Prerequisites: multiplication of algebraic terms and expanding a single bracket. A useful foundation before factorising quadratics. This is a focused Year 9 / KS3 worksheet, not an exam-board-specific paper; marks are suggested teaching guidance.

Key ideas at a glance

Divide every term by the common factor

For 12x² + 18x, take out 6x to obtain 6x(2x + 3). Both terms must be divided by the factor outside the bracket.

Expand to check

Multiplying the factor back through the bracket should reproduce the original expression. If a further common factor remains inside, the expression is not yet fully factorised.
